current.text: He joined Brooklyn from Minnesota in the Nic Claxton trade.
He is a projected starter for Brooklyn, next to Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr. and Day'Ron Sharpe.
He is the Nets' most accomplished on-ball creator and is expected to handle the ball a lot.
His usage should rise from about 27 to about 30, and his assists could go up. His defensive stats probably will not.
His minutes are expected to drop to about 32 per game because Brooklyn has little to play for. Blowouts and minutes for Noah Clowney also lower his upside.
Houston controls Brooklyn's draft pick, so the Nets have no reason to tank.
Brooklyn may still rest him or trim his minutes late in the season, mainly in March, to give young players time.
He has several years left on his contract and is expected to stay in Brooklyn.
Brooklyn is projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins.
The experts differ a little on his rank. One projects him 55 to 75 in category leagues, probably 65 to 70. Another says he can be top 50 again and calls him a value at 73.
His ESPN rank of 86 is great value and his Yahoo ADP near 68 is fine. In category leagues, take him a bit later than in points leagues.
In a mock auction, the expert hoped to get him for about 10 USD. He went for 15 USD.
His block rate could recover in Brooklyn now that he does not play next to Gobert.
Brooklyn has 16 back-to-backs, tied for the most in the league. Its playoff schedule for a March 28 end is 3-4-3 games, with one back-to-back.

durable.text: He is worth more in points leagues than in category leagues.
He turns the ball over a lot. Turnovers are his weakest category.
He gives little on defense. His blocks are poor and his steals are average.
His main strengths are points, rebounds and assists. His assists are high for a forward.
He shoots about 48% from the field and 80% from the line, so his percentages are close to neutral.
His shooting percentages swing from season to season and are hard to trust.
He shot 32% from three in Minnesota and was treated as a non-shooter.

note: Randle is a mid-round forward who gives points, rebounds and guard-like assists with neutral percentages. He costs you turnovers and defense, so he fits punt TO builds best. The experts rank him around 55 to 75 in category leagues, which matches his Yahoo rank of 71 and the 10 USD he cost in our league last season. Aim for about 10 to 12 USD and stop near the 15 USD he went for in the mock. Early on, check whether his usage really rises toward 30 and whether his minutes hold near 32. Plan for missed games in March and a thin 10-game playoff schedule.
